```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

# Read an existing report CSV safely
read_report_data <- function(filename) {
  if (file.exists(filename)) {
    read.csv(filename, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    NULL
  }
}

# Display a CSV table when available
show_table <- function(filename, caption, n = 10) {
  data <- read_report_data(filename)

  if (!is.null(data) && nrow(data) > 0) {
    cat("\n", caption, "\n")
    print(knitr::kable(
      head(data, n),
      caption = caption
    ))
  } else {
    cat("\nData file not available:", filename, "\n")
  }
}

# Display an existing chart when available
show_figure <- function(filename, caption) {
  if (file.exists(filename)) {
    cat("\n", caption, "\n")
    knitr::include_graphics(filename)
  } else {
    cat("\nChart not available:", filename, "\n")
  }
}
```

# Chapter 1: Executive Sales Performance Report

## 1.1 Business Problem

Retail managers need to understand overall sales performance, revenue generation, order activity, and sales trends.

This report evaluates the historical sales performance of Retail Pulse Kerala to support business planning and management decisions.

## 1.2 Dataset Description

The analysis uses the cleaned retail sales dataset containing 985,151 records.

Important fields include invoice details, invoice dates, product codes, quantities, and revenue.

## 1.3 Methodology

The analysis includes:
- Data cleaning and validation.
- Revenue and quantity calculations.
- Order and customer KPI analysis.
- Monthly revenue analysis.
- Sales trend visualization.

## 1.4 Analysis and Visualizations

### Sales KPI Summary

```{r}
show_table("kpi_summary.csv", "Overall Sales KPI Summary")
show_table("kpi_phase4.csv", "Phase 4 KPI Results")
```

### Monthly Revenue

```{r}
show_table("datatable_monthly_sales.csv", "Monthly Sales Summary")
show_figure("figures/01_monthly_revenue.png", "Monthly Revenue Trend")
show_figure("figures/02_mom_growth.png", "Month-on-Month Growth")
show_figure("figures/03_weekly_revenue.png", "Weekly Revenue")
```

### Product and Category Performance

```{r}
show_figure("figures/07_top10_products.png", "Top 10 Products")
show_figure("figures/12_category_donut.png", "Category Revenue Distribution")
show_table("product_profitability.csv", "Product Profitability")
```

## 1.5 Key Findings

The completed KPI analysis recorded:
- Total revenue: GBP 19,148,015.
- Total orders: 38,975.
- Average order value: GBP 491.
- Average selling price: GBP 1.75 per unit.
- Sales growth from January to November 2011 compared with the same period in 2010: 3%.

These are historical results from the project analysis.

## 1.6 Business Implications

Sales KPIs help managers understand revenue generation and purchasing activity. Monthly trends help identify periods of stronger or weaker performance.

## 1.7 Recommendations

- Monitor revenue and order KPIs regularly.
- Identify products contributing the most revenue.
- Investigate declining sales periods.
- Use historical sales trends for business planning.
- Review product profitability before making pricing decisions.

## 1.8 Limitations

- Historical sales do not guarantee future performance.
- Some customer information is missing.
- Cost information is available for only a portion of products.

## 2.2 Dataset Description

This analysis uses customer analytics outputs, including high-value customer information, churn predictions, customer segmentation visualizations, and reactivation recommendations.

## 2.5 Key Findings

The project generates customer segmentation, high-value customer records, and churn-risk predictions.

These outputs can help identify customers who may need additional engagement. Actual segment sizes and model performance should be interpreted using the displayed results.

## 2.6 Business Implications

Customer segmentation allows management to develop different strategies for valuable, active, and potentially inactive customers.

## 2.7 Recommendations

- Introduce loyalty programmes for high-value customers.

# Chapter 3: Inventory Optimization Report

## 3.1 Business Problem

Poor inventory management can cause stock shortages, excess inventory, and lost sales.

The purpose of this report is to evaluate inventory performance and support better stock replenishment decisions.

## 3.2 Dataset Description

The project uses product, inventory, sales, demand, supplier lead-time, and reorder recommendation outputs.

## 3.3 Methodology

The analysis includes:
- Inventory KPI calculations.
- Stock status evaluation.
- Inventory risk identification.
- Supplier lead-time analysis.
- Reorder recommendation analysis.

## 3.4 Analysis and Visualizations

### Inventory KPIs and Risk

```{r}
show_table("inventory_kpis.csv", "Inventory KPI Summary")
show_table("inventory_risk_full.csv", "Inventory Risk Details")
show_figure("figures/27_inventory_status.png", "Inventory Status")
show_figure("figures/28_top_risk.png", "Highest Inventory Risks")
```

### Stock and Supplier Analysis

```{r}
show_figure("figures/29_days_remaining.png", "Estimated Days of Stock Remaining")
show_figure("figures/30_supplier_lead_times.png", "Supplier Lead Times")
```

### Reorder Recommendations

```{r}
show_table("reorder_recommendations.csv", "Reorder Recommendations")
show_table("forecast_reorder_recommendations.csv", "Forecast-Based Reorder Recommendations")
```

## 3.5 Key Findings

The inventory analysis generates stock-status information, inventory risk records, and reorder recommendations.

The results help identify products that may require replenishment or closer monitoring.

## 3.6 Business Implications

Inventory analysis helps managers reduce stock shortages, avoid unnecessary stock accumulation, and improve product availability.

## 3.7 Recommendations

- Monitor products with high inventory risk.
- Review reorder recommendations regularly.
- Consider supplier lead times when planning purchases.
- Maintain appropriate safety stock.
- Compare actual demand with inventory levels.

## 3.8 Limitations

- Inventory recommendations depend on the accuracy of stock records.
- Supplier lead times may change.
- Forecasted demand may differ from actual demand.

# Chapter 4: Demand Forecasting and Model Evaluation Report

## 4.1 Business Problem

Retailers need to estimate future product demand to plan stock levels, purchasing, and business operations.

This report evaluates historical demand patterns and forecasting model outputs.

## 4.2 Dataset Description

The analysis uses historical daily sales and demand-related features, model comparison outputs, forecast results, and product demand classifications.

## 4.3 Methodology

The forecasting workflow includes:
- Historical demand analysis.
- Time-series visualization.
- Feature preparation.
- Forecast model comparison.
- Model evaluation.
- Future demand estimation.

## 4.4 Analysis and Visualizations

### Demand Patterns

```{r}
show_table("daily_series.csv", "Daily Demand Data")
show_figure("figures/31_decomposition.png", "Demand Decomposition")
show_figure("figures/32_weekly_units.png", "Weekly Demand")
```

### Forecast Model Evaluation

```{r}
show_table("forecast_model_comparison.csv", "Forecast Model Comparison")
show_table("best_model_per_horizon.csv", "Best Model by Forecast Horizon")
show_figure("figures/33_model_comparison.png", "Forecast Model Performance")
show_figure("figures/34_actual_vs_predicted.png", "Actual versus Predicted Demand")
```

### Future Demand Forecast

```{r}
show_table("forecast_7_day.csv", "Seven-Day Forecast")
show_table("forecast_30_day.csv", "Thirty-Day Forecast")
show_table("forecast_next90_days.csv", "Ninety-Day Forecast")
show_figure("figures/35_forecast_90_day.png", "Ninety-Day Demand Forecast")
```

### Product Demand Classification

```{r}
show_table("product_demand_classes.csv", "Product Demand Classes")
show_figure("figures/38_demand_classes.png", "Demand Classification")
```

## 4.5 Key Findings

The project generates short-term and longer-term forecasts, compares forecasting models, and classifies product demand.

The model comparison results should be used to identify the most suitable model for each forecast horizon.

## 4.6 Business Implications

Demand forecasts can help managers plan purchasing, inventory replenishment, and stock availability.

## 4.7 Recommendations

- Use forecast results as planning support.
- Monitor forecast accuracy regularly.
- Compare predicted demand with actual sales.
- Review demand patterns before placing large orders.
- Update models when new sales data becomes available.

## 4.8 Limitations

- Forecast accuracy depends on historical data quality.
- Unexpected market changes may affect actual demand.
- Forecasts are estimates, not guaranteed sales results.

# Chapter 5: Anomaly Detection Report

## 5.1 Business Problem

Unusual sales patterns may indicate unexpected demand changes, transaction issues, or operational problems.

Anomaly detection helps managers identify unusual observations that require further investigation.

## 5.2 Dataset Description

This analysis uses cleaned retail transaction data and the anomaly detection outputs generated by the project.

## 5.3 Methodology

The workflow includes:
- Data preparation.
- Selection of relevant sales variables.
- Anomaly identification.
- Alert generation.
- Visualization of unusual observations.

## 5.4 Analysis and Visualizations

### Anomaly Alerts

```{r}
show_table("anomaly_alerts.csv", "Detected Anomaly Alerts", 20)
```

### Anomaly Visualization

```{r}
show_figure("figures/39_anomalies.png", "Anomaly Detection Results")
```

### Data Quality

```{r}
show_table("data_quality_report.csv", "Data Quality Report")
show_table("rejection_reasons.csv", "Data Rejection Reasons")
```

## 5.5 Key Findings

The project produces anomaly alerts and visualizations to highlight unusual observations.

Each flagged observation should be reviewed before deciding whether it represents a genuine business issue.

## 5.6 Business Implications

Anomaly detection can support early investigation of unusual transaction patterns and help improve operational monitoring.

## 5.7 Recommendations

- Review flagged anomalies regularly.
- Investigate unusual revenue and quantity patterns.
- Check suspicious records against source transactions.
- Maintain data validation procedures.
- Record the reason for each investigated alert.

## 5.8 Limitations

- An anomaly is not necessarily an error or fraud.
- Detection depends on the selected method and thresholds.
- Unusual but genuine business events may also be flagged.

# Chapter 6: Final Business Recommendations Report

## 6.1 Business Problem

Retail managers need a consolidated view of sales, customers, inventory, demand, and unusual business patterns.

This chapter combines the project outputs into practical business recommendations.

## 6.2 Dataset Description

This report uses the cleaned sales dataset and the generated sales, customer, inventory, forecasting, and anomaly analysis outputs.

## 6.3 Methodology

The recommendations are based on:
- Sales KPI analysis.
- Customer segmentation and churn analysis.
- Inventory risk analysis.
- Demand forecasting.
- Anomaly detection.

## 6.4 Analysis and Visualizations

### Business Recommendation Summary

```{r}
show_table("recommendation_summary.csv", "Recommendation Summary")
show_table("recommendations.csv", "Business Recommendations")
show_figure("figures/40_recommendations_by_type.png", "Recommendations by Type")
```

### Sales and Customer Performance

```{r}
show_table("kpi_summary.csv", "Sales KPI Summary")
show_table("high_value_customers.csv", "High-Value Customers")
```

### Inventory and Forecasting

```{r}
show_table("inventory_kpis.csv", "Inventory KPI Summary")
show_table("forecast_model_comparison.csv", "Forecast Model Comparison")
```

## 6.5 Key Findings

The project provides analytical outputs across five important areas:

1. Sales performance and revenue trends.
2. Customer value and churn risk.
3. Inventory status and stock risk.
4. Demand forecasting and model evaluation.
5. Anomaly alerts and data quality.

These outputs provide a foundation for evidence-based retail decisions.

## 6.6 Business Implications

Combining the analytical results helps management understand how sales, customers, stock availability, and demand are connected.

## 6.7 Final Recommendations

- Monitor sales KPIs through regular dashboards.
- Develop targeted strategies for different customer groups.
- Improve inventory replenishment using demand forecasts.
- Review high-risk inventory items.
- Investigate unusual transaction patterns.
- Evaluate model performance regularly.
- Refresh datasets and reports periodically.

## 6.8 Limitations

- Findings depend on the quality and completeness of the available datasets.
- Forecasting and prediction models have uncertainty.
- Some cost and customer information may be incomplete.
- Recommendations should be reviewed alongside actual business conditions.

---

# Conclusion

Retail Pulse Kerala demonstrates how data analytics can support retail business decisions.

The project combines data cleaning, exploratory analysis, KPI calculation, customer analytics, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and business recommendations.

The final reports translate technical analysis into information that retail managers can use for planning and decision-making.
